RESPONDENT/COMPLAINANT Counsel for the Petitioner/accused:
1. SUBBA RAO KORRAPATI Counsel for the Respondent/complainant:
1. PUBLIC PROSECUTOR (AP)

The Court made the following:
This Criminal Petition under Sections 437 and 439 of Cr.P.C., has been filed by the petitioner/accused No.1 seeking regular bail in Crime No.91 of 2024 of Jaggaiahpet Police Station, NTR District.
2.

The above said crime was registered against the petitioner/accused No.1 and another for the offences punishable under Sections 376(1), 506 r/w 34 IPC.
3.

The case of the prosecution in brief is that victim is resident of Mittagudem of Jaggaiahpeta,
studied MBA in 2021.
She has been working as Senior Officer in Credit Card Department, ICICI Towers, Hyderabad.
By that time, she got friendship with accused No.1 who is resident of Balusupadu and he was also working as Civil Engineer in Hyderabad.
Accused No.1 told the victim that he would marry her.
On VJP,J believing the words of accused No.1, she moved closely with him.
On 20.01.2024 at 2.30 pm accused No.1 took the victim to his room and forcibly enjoyed her, though she denied on 10.3.2024 at 3.00 pm.
In view of Sivaratri festival, when the victim went to her house at Jaggaiahpeta.
Accused No.1 came to the house of victim and enjoyed her physically, during temporary absence of the inmates of her house.
When the victim asked the accused No.1 to marry her, he denied.
Then victim informed the same to the parents of accused No.1.
By that time, A1 and his parents threatened the victim and her parents with dire consequences.
Basing on the complaint of the victim a case was registered.

4. Heard Sri Subba Rao Korrapati, learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Assistant Vallepu Srikanth vs State Of Andhra Pradesh on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40796827/
1 Prosecutor representing the State/Respondent.

sentences.text: Perused the entire material on record.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the petitioner and the victim both are adults working at Hyderabad in different offices and they fall in love.
Thereafter, due to some misunderstandings and differences, this case has been lodged.
The petitioner has been in judicial custody since 15.04.2024.
Investigation is almost completed.
Learned counsel for the petitioner prays to release the petitioner on regular bail.
VJP,J 6.
Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor submits that investigation is completed.
It is pending for RFSL report and prays to pass appropriate orders.

7. Considering the submissions made, taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case, the background in which the alleged incident occurred and as reported, the investigation is completed and there is no chance to complete trial within a reasonable period of time and hence, it is desirable to release the petitioner on bail.
8.

In the result, the Criminal Petition is allowed with the following conditions:
i.

The petitioner herein shall be released on bail on his executing a personal bond for Rs.20,000/- (Rupees twenty thousand only) with two (02) sureties for a like sum each to the satisfaction of the Court of Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class,
Jaggaiah Peta, NTR District.

entities.text:
Court of Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class,
Jaggaiah Peta, NTR District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: ii. On release, the petitioner shall appear before the Station House Officer, concerned, once in a week i.e., on every Sunday between 10.00 a.m. and 05.00 p.m., till the filing of charge sheet.
iii. The petitioner is directed not to hamper the investigation and tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
VJP,J iv.

It is made clear that the petitioner shall scrupulously comply with the above conditions and breach of any of the above conditions will be viewed seriously and prosecution is at liberty to move an application for cancellation of the bail.
As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
